title: Note without a Print Reference Mark

illustrates.quote: The embedded note must be on the same line as at least one word or phrase to which it applies. Note: Do not confuse marginal notes with sidebars. (See Formats, §12, Sidebars.)

blocks.text: That floating stuff is called slag. The slag is then skimmed off.
blocks.features: Plain body text, no reference symbol or emphasis marking the word "slag".

blocks.text: Slag is the dross of metal
blocks.features: Set in the right margin, in italic type, alongside the body paragraph -- a genuine marginal note with no print symbol connecting it to a specific word.

braille.notes: Per rule 16.4b, the embedded transcriber's note reads literally "note" (not the marginal note's actual text) enclosed in transcriber's-note indicators (@.< ... @.>), inserted after "slag" on the same braille line -- the point of reference -- rather than reproducing the marginal note's wording inline. The margin note's actual text ("Slag is the dross of metal") is not itself shown transcribed anywhere in this two-line excerpt.

uncertain: The excerpt shown does not include where/whether the marginal note's actual wording ("Slag is the dross of metal") is transcribed elsewhere on this braille page; only the embedded placeholder note is visible in this two-line box.
resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.4.c per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: verified directly: line 12476, stripped of its 9-space left padding, is exactly 40 characters, ending in the embedded TN indicator. braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
